title: A quadratic alphabet threshold for non-overlapping codes
description: For length-n non-overlapping (cross-bifix-free) codes, let q₀(n) be the least alphabet size beyond which a Blackburn split is always maximum. We prove q₀(n) = n²/2 + O(n), with q₀(n) ≤ 4n(n−1) for n ≥ 3. A family of non-overlapping codes yields exceptional alphabets for every n ≥ 12. A length-six code on nine symbols has 33,851 words, while the best Blackburn split has 33,614, disproving Conjecture 1 of Stanovnik, Moškon and Mraz. We also determine the maximum for all alphabets at length five. The archive includes the research preprint, its LaTeX source, formal proofs in Lean 4, and a verification report.
